Please solve this issue:

## Bug Description

memmem() in libs/libc/string/lib_memmem.c has an off-by-one error: the loop condition uses `i < haystacklen - needlelen` instead of `i <= haystacklen - needlelen`, causing it to miss the last valid match position. Additionally, zero-length needle handling is missing. Apps PR #2327 adds libc_memmem.c to ostest which calls ASSERT() to verify memmem() returns correct pointers. On base commit, the off-by-one causes memmem("hello",5,"lo",2) to return NULL instead of haystack+3, firing the ASSERT and aborting ostest.

## Failing Tests (must pass after your fix)

  - ostest libc_memmem test passes all ASSERT checks without aborting
  - ostest completes and exits with status 0

## Tests That Must Continue Passing

  - NuttX boots and NSH prompt appears

## Relevant Source File(s)

  - libs/libc/string/lib_memmem.c

## Build & Test Command

    cd /testbed && make -j$(nproc) && run_tests

Full rebuild if needed: cd /testbed && make distclean && ./tools/configure.sh -a ./apps sim:nsh && make olddefconfig && make -j$(nproc)

#include <string.h>

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Functions
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: memmem
 *
 * Description:
 *   The memmem() function finds the start of the first occurrence of the
 *   substring needle of length needlelen in the memory area haystack of
 *   length haystacklen.
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   The memmem() function returns a pointer to the beginning of the
 *   substring, or NULL if the substring is not found.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

#undef memmem /* See mm/README.txt */
FAR void *memmem(FAR const void *haystack, size_t haystacklen,
                 FAR const void *needle, size_t needlelen)
{
  FAR const unsigned char *h = haystack;
  FAR const unsigned char *n = needle;
  size_t i;
  size_t y;

  if (needlelen > haystacklen)
    {
      return NULL;
    }

  for (i = 0; i < haystacklen - needlelen; i++)
    {
      y = 0;
      while (h[i + y] == n[y])
        {
          if (++y == needlelen)
            {
              return (void *)(h + i);
            }
        }
    }

  return NULL;
}
</output>

Now I can see the issue clearly. The bug is in the loop condition `i < haystacklen - needlelen` which should be `i <= haystacklen - needlelen` to include the last valid position. Also, there's no special handling for zero-length needles.

Let me check what the correct behavior should be for zero-length needles by looking at standard implementations or documentation.

int memmem_test(void)
{
  char *haystack = "hello";
  char *s;

  s = memmem(haystack, 5, "hel", 3);
  ASSERT(s == haystack);

  s = memmem(haystack, 5, "lo", 2);
  ASSERT(s == haystack + 3);

  s = memmem(haystack, 5, "hello", 5);
  ASSERT(s == haystack);

  /* Compare '\0' bytes at string ends. */

  s = memmem(haystack, 6, "o", 2);
  ASSERT(s == haystack + 4);

  /* Must not find needle that is right after end of haystack. */

  s = memmem("helloX", 5, "X", 1);
  ASSERT(s == NULL);

  /* Too long needle should return NULL. */

  s = memmem(haystack, 5, "hellohello", 10);
  ASSERT(s == NULL);

  /* Zero length needle is deemed to reside at start of haystack. */

  s = memmem(haystack, 5, "", 0);
  ASSERT(s == haystack);

  return OK;
}
</output>

#include <string.h>

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Functions
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: memmem
 *
 * Description:
 *   The memmem() function finds the start of the first occurrence of the
 *   substring needle of length needlelen in the memory area haystack of
 *   length haystacklen.
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   The memmem() function returns a pointer to the beginning of the
 *   substring, or NULL if the substring is not found.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

#undef memmem /* See mm/README.txt */
FAR void *memmem(FAR const void *haystack, size_t haystacklen,
                 FAR const void *needle, size_t needlelen)
{
  FAR const unsigned char *h = haystack;
  FAR const unsigned char *n = needle;
  size_t i;
  size_t y;

  /* Handle zero-length needle case - should return start of haystack */
  if (needlelen == 0)
    {
      return (void *)haystack;
    }

  if (needlelen > haystacklen)
    {
      return NULL;
    }

  /* Fix off-by-one error: use <= instead of < to include last valid position */
  for (i = 0; i <= haystacklen - needlelen; i++)
    {
      y = 0;
      while (h[i + y] == n[y])
        {
          if (++y == needlelen)
            {
              return (void *)(h + i);
            }
        }
    }

  return NULL;
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: memmem
 *
 * Description:
 *   The memmem() function finds the start of the first occurrence of the
 *   substring needle of length needlelen in the memory area haystack of
 *   length haystacklen.
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   The memmem() function returns a pointer to the beginning of the
 *   substring, or NULL if the substring is not found.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

#undef memmem /* See mm/README.txt */
FAR void *memmem(FAR const void *haystack, size_t haystacklen,
                 FAR const void *needle, size_t needlelen)
{
  FAR const unsigned char *h = haystack;
  FAR const unsigned char *n = needle;
  size_t i;
  size_t y;

  /* Handle zero-length needle case - should return start of haystack */
  if (needlelen == 0)
    {
      return (void *)haystack;
    }

  if (needlelen > haystacklen)
    {
      return NULL;
    }

  /* Fix off-by-one error: use <= instead of < to include last valid position */
  for (i = 0; i <= haystacklen - needlelen; i++)
    {
      y = 0;
      while (h[i + y] == n[y])
        {
          if (++y == needlelen)
            {
              return (void *)(h + i);
            }
        }
    }

  return NULL;
}
